predecessors.name: Moche culture
predecessors.text: the Moche, Chicama and Virú valleys: 'The culture arose about 900 CE, succeeding the Moche culture'

ledger.x: c. 900: the Chimú arise at Chan Chan in the Moche valley. 'The culture arose about 900 CE, succeeding the Moche culture'; infobox 'Established c. 900'; Chan Chan 'was the capital of the historical empire of the Chimor from 900 to 1470' (Chan Chan page). The page's Chimú oral history gives Taycanamo, who arrives 'from…

c. 1320: Chimor conquers the Jequetepeque valley. 'The Chimú conquered the Jequetepeque around 1320 and changed the political structure of the society'; Farfán in the valley became 'a subordinate' of Chan Chan.
ledger.cp: Jequetepeque valley societies (unnamed on the page)

ledger.x: c. 1370: Ñancempinco expands Chimor north and south. 'Ñançenpinco began further expansion both north and south of the Moche Valleys' and 'laid the foundations of the Kingdom by conquering ... the neighboring valleys of Sana, Pacasmayo, Chicama, Viru, Chao and Santa'; he 'was believed to have ruled around 1370'…
ledger.cp: Zaña, Chao and Santa valley societies (unnamed on the page)

ledger.x: Chimor reaches Carabayllo on the south.
1375: Chimor conquers the Sicán heartland of Lambayeque.
The north coast to Tumbes joins Chimor.
1470: Chimor ends, 'the largest polity conquered by the Inca'; its land goes to the Inca Empire.

wars.name: Chimú conquest of the Jequetepeque
wars.outcome: Chimor takes the Jequetepeque valley c.

wars.name: Chimú expansion under Ñancempinco
wars.outcome: Ñancempinco conquers the valleys north and south of the Moche valley; the southern limit is Carabayllo, where the 'great valley of Lima' stopped Chimor.

wars.name: Chimú conquest of Lambayeque
wars.outcome: Chimor conquers the Late Sicán heartland of Lambayeque circa 1375.

wars.name: Inca conquest of Chimor
wars.outcome: Topa Inca Yupanqui defeats Minchançaman; Chimor is incorporated into the Inca Empire in 1470 (infobox).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line: the valley limits are the pages' valley names and a coast measured in km; the Lima-valley limit at Carabayllo and the Tumbes limit are the softest.
